D.immediate_priority: Receive the next genuinely available seat so the carried meal can be eaten.
D.initial_observation: Sees A return, B occupying the disputed seat, and C still using the other seat.
D.interaction_style: Brief and opportunistic about genuinely free seats. You may volunteer a relevant firsthand fact once, but do not act as a mediator or narrate an action everyone just observed.
D.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
D.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
D.private_knowledge: Saw A place the tissue packet on the disputed seat earlier but did not see B arrive or move it.
D.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.
D.role: Standing diner waiting for a seat

scenario.implementation_notes: Agents have no physical actions and the environment reports no state, so any arrangement exists only in the conversation. No scenario text or shared prompt text states or models a duration, deadline, or clock. Identical to S23 otherwise, including the shared notice that the conversation ends in some settled arrangement. S25 additionally switches the shared prompt to speech-only wording and replaces the hard-constraint priority rule with a priced-preference rule.
scenario.observation_focus: Whether the reservation claim, present occupancy, spill risk, and waiting diner create expressed conflict; how any concrete arrangement distributes the practical costs.
scenario.resolution_expectation: However this conversation goes, it will end with everyone here having settled on some arrangement they are each willing to go along with, even if it is not anyone's first choice. What that arrangement is, who adjusts, what is asked in return, and when it is reached are for you to work out by talking.
scenario.shared_setting: A busy Singapore hawker centre at lunchtime Every table currently visible to the four people is full. At a small two-seat table, Casey occupies one seat and the other is occupied by Jamie. There are no loose chairs and no room to add one without blocking the aisle. A small unopened tissue packet rests beside Jamie. The four people are strangers and have not spoken before.
scenario.shared_trigger: Alex arrives carrying a hot meal and stops at the only disputed seat. Jamie has already placed a tray and uncovered a bowl there. Casey remains in the other seat, while Robin stands nearby carrying food and waiting for whichever seat next becomes available. No one has moved or offered a concrete arrangement yet.
scenario.source_status: S24 plus a speech-only shared prompt and a priced-preference priority rule
